name: Magnolia
why_it_matters: Sit-down multi-cuisine restaurant near Castairs Town — TripAdvisor ranks it among the top 5 of 38 Deoghar restaurants. One of the few dinner options in the temple-town that serves chicken alongside a vegetarian menu.
insider_tip: Pilgrim crowd skips this for pure-veg bhojanalayas, so weeknight dinners are quieter than the Tower Chowk strip.
signature_address: Bihari Lal Chakravorty Road, Near Castairs Town, Deoghar 814112

name: Nirvana Rooftop Cafe
why_it_matters: Rooftop cafe at The Magnum Hotel on S.B. Roy Road, near the Jain temple — one of the rare cafes in Deoghar serving Italian alongside snacks. Walking distance from both the temple complex and the hotel cluster around Tower Chowk.
insider_tip: Sunset visit (5-6 pm) gives a clear view across Castairs Town rooftops — best window for the cafe's outdoor seating.
signature_address: The Magnum Hotel, Near Jain Mandir, S.B. Roy Road, Castairs Town, Deoghar 814112

name: Hotel Yashoda International Restaurant
why_it_matters: In-house multi-cuisine restaurant of Hotel Yashoda International — a Tower Chowk landmark within walking distance of Baba Baidyanath temple. Open to non-guests and one of the few sit-down options very close to the temple complex.
insider_tip: Pure-veg menu rules during Shravan (July-August) when the entire town goes vegetarian for the kanwar yatra crowd.

name: Chamari Sah Mistaan Bhandar
why_it_matters: Counter sweet shop in the Baidyanath Dham temple zone, operating since 1995. Peda — Deoghar's signature sweet, a dense khoya-and-sugar disc tied to the temple's prasad culture — is the headline product alongside the standard mithai range.
insider_tip: Buy peda hot from the morning trays (9-11 am); afternoon stock dries out and loses the soft-grain texture pilgrims pack home.
